Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.7 · Exercise 40

Mass and Center of Mass of a Solid with a Parabolic Roof Line

Problem

Find the mass and the center of mass of the solid E with density ρ(x,y,z)=4. The solid E is bounded by the parabolic cylinder z=1−y2 and by the planes x+z=1, x=0, and z=0.

m=∭E​4dV.

Reading the solid

The plane x+z=1 gives x=1−z. The plane x=0 closes the solid on the back. Together they say that the x-coordinate is trapped between two surfaces:

0≤x≤1−z.

The inequality x≥0 is already true, so the upper limit 1−z must be nonnegative. That condition gives z≤1. The parabolic cylinder adds the second ceiling:

0≤z≤1−y2.

The number 1−y2 is nonnegative only when ∣y∣≤1. The projection of E onto the yz-plane is therefore the parabolic segment D={(y,z):−1≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y2}, and the solid is the set

E={(x,y,z):−1≤y≤1,0≤z≤1−y2,0≤x≤1−z}.

A second reading is shorter. Hold y fixed. The section of E in the plane of constant y is the right triangle with vertices (0,y,0), (1,y,0), and (0,y,1−y2). Its horizontal leg has length 1, its vertical leg has length 1−y2, and its hypotenuse lies on the plane x+z=1. The triangle shrinks to a point as y approaches ±1.

No coordinate change is needed. The bounds are flat in x, and the volume element is dV=dxdzdy. The density is the constant 4, so the mass is

m=∫−11​∫01−y2​∫01−z​4dxdzdy.

Solution

Step 1 — Integrate with respect to x

The density is constant, so the innermost integral is the length of the fibre in the x-direction:

∫01−z​4dx=4(1−z).

Step 2 — Integrate with respect to z

Put a=1−y2 for the height of the triangle. The z-integral runs from 0 to a:

∫0a​4(1−z)dz=4[z−2z2​]0a​=4(a−2a2​).

Now a−a2/2=(1−y2)−(1−2y2+y4)/2=(1−y4)/2, hence

∫01−y2​4(1−z)dz=2(1−y4).

Step 3 — Integrate with respect to y

The integrand is even in y, so the integral over −1≤y≤1 is twice the integral over 0≤y≤1:

m=∫−11​2(1−y4)dy=2[y−5y5​]−11​=2⋅2⋅(1−51​)=516​.

The mass is 16/5=3.2.

Step 4 — Moment about the yz-plane

The first moment about the yz-plane weights each point by its distance x from that plane:

Myz​=∭E​4xdV=∫−11​∫01−y2​∫01−z​4xdxdzdy.

The inner integral is 2(1−z)2. With a=1−y2,

∫0a​2(1−z)2dz=2[a−a2+3a3​]=2⋅31−y6​,

because a−a2+a3/3=(1−y6)/3 after the substitution u=y2. Then

Myz​=32​∫−11​(1−y6)dy=32​⋅2⋅(1−71​)=78​.

Step 5 — Moment about the xz-plane

The solid and the density are unchanged when y is replaced by −y: the cylinder z=1−y2 and the three planes do not distinguish the sign of y. The integrand 4y is odd in y, and the y-limits are symmetric, so

Mxz​=∭E​4ydV=0.

Step 6 — Moment about the xy-plane

For the moment about the floor, the inner integral is ∫01−z​4zdx=4z(1−z):

∫0a​4z(1−z)dz=4[2z2​−3z3​]0a​=4(2a2​−3a3​).

Substitute a=1−y2 and expand in powers of y:

2a2​−3a3​=61​−2y4​+3y6​,
Mxy​=4∫−11​(61​−2y4​+3y6​)dy=8(61​−101​+211​)=8⋅354​=3532​.

Step 7 — Divide each moment by the mass

The coordinates of the center of mass are the moments divided by m=16/5:

xˉ=mMyz​​=16/58/7​=145​,yˉ​=mMxz​​=0,zˉ=mMxy​​=16/532/35​=72​.

The value xˉ=5/14≈0.357 is less than 1/2. That is reasonable: the solid is thickest at z=0, where the fibre runs the full length 1, and it narrows to zero thickness at z=1. The value zˉ=2/7≈0.286 is less than 1/2 for the same reason, because the solid carries most of its volume low down.

Answer

m=516​=3.2,(xˉ,yˉ​,zˉ)=(145​,0,72​)≈(0.357,0,0.286).

Notation

SymbolMeaning
∭E​fdVThe triple integral of f over the solid E; it is the limit of sums of f times small volumes.
EThe solid region of integration, that is, the set of points that satisfy the stated inequalities.
dVThe volume element. Here dV=dxdzdy, because the three coordinates are integrated in that order.
ρ(x,y,z)The density, here the constant 4. In this exercise the units are mass per unit volume.
z=1−y2A parabolic cylinder: the parabola z=1−y2 in the yz-plane, translated along the x-axis.
x+z=1A plane that cuts the solid on the front and forms the hypotenuse of every triangular section.
Myz​,Mxz​,Mxy​The first moments of mass about the coordinate planes. Myz​=∭xρdV measures the pull toward the yz-plane.
xˉ,yˉ​,zˉThe coordinates of the center of mass, Myz​/m, Mxz​/m, Mxy​/m.
aShorthand for the height 1−y2 of the triangular section at a fixed y.

Verification

Four scripts confirm the result.

  • part1_step1.py checks the inequalities and estimates the mass by Monte Carlo sampling of the box 0≤x≤1, −1≤y≤1, 0≤z≤1. It reports 3.20015 against 16/5=3.2, a deviation of 0.08 standard errors.
  • part1_step2.py repeats the mass integral in SymPy and obtains 16/5. It also prints the intermediate results 4−4z and 2−2y4.
  • part1_step3.py evaluates the three moments in SymPy and obtains 8/7, 0, and 32/35, hence the center of mass (5/14,0,2/7).
  • part1_step4.py integrates in the reverse order, with x outermost and y innermost, using mpmath. It confirms m=3.2, Myz​=1.14285714285714, Mxz​=0, and Mxy​=0.914285714285714.
